title: SLO runway experiment journal — microcycles & cross‑team playbook
content:
Purpose and framing:

This is a lightweight, tactical notebook for running a series of short SLO experiments across product, backend, serving-runtime, and SRE. Our goal is to validate a repeatable 6-week microcycle for SLO discovery -> automation -> validation -> handoff. This doc is intentionally practical: play-by-play decisions, meeting notes, risks, and action items.

High-level objectives (what success looks like for the microcycle):
- Validate an SLO candidate for the Hosted Text Generation API route '/v1/generate' that balances error budget with latency and cost.
- Automate collection of three high-fidelity signals (p95 latency, 99th token-generation latency, and user-impacting error rate) into a per-route dashboard and daily alert.
- Prove a rollback and canary policy integration with rollout automation (feature flag + route fallback) in staging.
- Produce a runbook snippet and a one-page handoff for Product + Support.

Scope (in/out):
- In: one primary route (generate), evaluation on production-like traffic in dedicated staging and canary in limited prod, cross-team oncall rehearsals, SLIs -> templated SLO docs.
- Out: platform-wide SLO rollout, quota/price changes, deep kernel/runtime optimization (this is an ops+signals experiment, not a performance optimization project).

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Product (Priya Shah): define user-impact thresholds, customer risk appetite, prioritize the route and feature-flag windows.
- Serving Runtime (Diego Alvarez): ensure tagging of requests, KV-cache visibility, and expose the token-level timing metric.
- Observability (Marcus Lee): implement dashboards, dashboards query tests, and alerting rules.
- SRE / Oncall (Sophie Chen): runbook authoring, incident simulation, and lead the canary rollback drills.
- Solutions/Support (Ethan Brooks): craft customer-facing communication and validation with CS for expected user behavior.

Success metrics (quantitative):
- Instrumentation completeness: 3 signals captured in dashboard for >= 95% of requests in staging within 2 weeks.
- Detection time: alert to page <= 5 minutes for a triggered 10-minute p95 latency spike.
- Recovery time objective for canary rollback drill: full route fallback executed and verified within 12 minutes.
- Validation: post-mortem of the canary drill with at least 2 identified process improvements and an updated runbook.

6-week microcycle roadmap (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (preparatory week): align stakeholders, finalize success metrics, create minimal acceptance criteria, and reserve staging capacity.
- Week 1: instrumentation sprint — add token-level timing and user-impact error tags; smoke tests.
- Week 2: observability sprint — dashboard templates, automated query tests, set alert thresholds, define noise reduction rules.
- Week 3: canary + traffic shaping — deploy canary routing for 1% traffic in staging, run synthetic load and golden-signature checks.
- Week 4: rehearsal & failure injection — SRE executes table-top and then live rollback drills; measure detection -> action -> verification time.
- Week 5: analysis & handoff — compile findings, update runbook, produce one-pager for Product and Support, schedule training.
- Week 6: buffer & rinse — address leftover infra bugs, extend to a second route if fast path validated.

Meeting rhythm and rituals:
- Twice-weekly 30m sync (Mon/Wed) for blockers, telemetry, and action updates. Owner rotates weekly (obs -> runtime -> SRE).
- Friday 60m demo + notes: share dashboard snapshots, replay canary artifacts, and capture learnings.
- Pre-canary checklist review: 15m signoff meeting with Product + SRE before any prod-facing rollout.

Instrumentation details (practical notes):
- New metrics to emit: request.token_gen_ms (histogram by token position), request.route_user_error (counter with reason tags), request.kv_cache_hit (boolean tag).
- Tagging policy: route, model_variant, tenant_id (if present), token_position_bucket (0–64, 65–256, 256+), and backend_node_id.
- Sampling: full sampling in staging; adaptive sampling in prod (first N requests per minute + 1% tail sampling).

Dashboard & alerting design patterns:
- Always show context: deployment id, model version, active rollout percentage.
- Alert 1 (latency red): p95 sustained > threshold for 10m -> page SRE.
- Alert 2 (token tail): 99th token latency > threshold and correlated with errors -> page runtime + SRE.
- Alert 3 (user-impact error): spike in request.route_user_error beyond normal baseline -> page oncall + product.
- Triage dashboard view includes correlated charts: token latency, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and recent error traces.

Runbook outline (short):
1) Detection: which alert fired and quick sanity checks (deploy window, model version).
2) Scoped mitigation: enable route fallback to earlier model variant, reduce concurrency on canary, pause feature flag.
3) Verification: run synthetic against fallback and validate user-facing sample.
4) Postmortem triage: collect traces, timeline, and update one-pager.

Canary & rollout automation notes:
- Canary determination: start 1% -> 5% -> 20% increments with 30m observation windows.
- Safety gates: automatic rollback if any pageable alert fires in observation window or if p99 latency increases > 2x baseline.
- Implementation: feature-flag + smart routing policy that can pivot to dedicated fallback pool (low-latency older model).

Risk register (top-level):
- Risk: telemetry gaps in token-level timing. Mitigation: early instrumentation spike tests and validation harness.
- Risk: alert noise causes alert fatigue. Mitigation: run a 48h alert quiet period with only high-confidence paging rules enabled.
- Risk: customer impact during canary rollout. Mitigation: start with internal-only tenants and synthetic traffic; CS ready to throttle.

Data and measurement plan:
- Store one-minute rollups for 90d and full histograms for 7d for deep dives.
- Weekly automated SLO burn reports for stakeholders (dashboard + email).
- Define baselines from last 30 days of staging-like traffic; store the baseline snapshot in confluence link above.

Communications and escalation:
- On-call paging follows existing SRE escalation policy.
- Public status template for CS: brief description, affected route, mitigation steps, ETA for fix. Draft stored in linked_artifacts.
- Internal incident channel: #ops-slo-runway (create ephemeral thread per canary).

Open questions & decisions to make:
- Exact numeric SLO thresholds: Product to propose two candidate thresholds by week 0.
- Token-level histogram retention cost: finance to sign off on budget for extended retention.
- Should we treat model variant changes as separate SLOs or variants under the same SLO? Decision due week 2.

Action items (first 14 days — owners + due dates):
- [Anika] Finalize experiment charter and acceptance criteria — due 2026-11-12.
- [Diego] Add token_gen_ms histogram and deployment tag to staging tracer — due 2026-11-19.
- [Marcus] Create dashboard template and synthetic query tests; wire up email digest — due 2026-11-22.
- [Sophie] Draft runbook snippet and run the first table-top rehearsal — due 2026-11-24.
- [Priya] Propose SLO candidate numbers and customer risk notes — due 2026-11-12.

Stubbed meeting notes (space for capture):
- 2026-11-09 sync: agreed on token buckets; Priya to propose threshold options.
- 2026-11-12 kickoff: staging capacity reserved; Marcus to provision dashboard space.

Postmortem template pointers (to use after drills):
- What happened (timeline), why it happened (root cause hypothesis), detection timeline, mitigation steps taken, impact quantification (customers, error budget burned), follow-up actions with owners, and retrospective notes.

Next steps (short):
1) Circulate this notebook with stakeholders and request sign-off on acceptance criteria.
2) Stand up instrumentation branch and run smoke tests in staging this week.
3) Schedule the canary dry-run and tabletop for Wk3.

Notes to self / working ideas (scratchpad):
- Consider adding a secondary SLI for "meaningful latency" defined at token 64 (end of short prompts) and token 512 (long prompts) to catch degradation patterns.
- If retention cost is high, explore storing full histograms only for sampled tenants and rollups for everyone else.
- Experiment with alert dedup window using request.trace_id to avoid duplicate pages from multiple correlated alerts.

Document history and change log:
- 2026-11-08: created (Anika) initial charter and microcycle plan.
- 2026-11-09: added stakeholder list and meeting rhythm.
- 2026-11-12: updated acceptance criteria after product kickoff.
- 2027-02-18: major update to canary gating logic and retention notes (Anika).

End of notebook — keep this doc as the canonical working journal for the microcycle. Add dated entries under "Meeting notes" as the experiment moves forward.
